subproblem.title: Integrals over C¹-close bi-Lipschitz images of a compact parameter set converge
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E := ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Amb n ℓ) and H := μHE[n], the n-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure on E. Let K ⊆ ℝⁿ (Rn n) be compact, let pr : E → ℝⁿ and L : ℝⁿ → E be continuous linear maps with pr(L v) = v for all v ∈ ℝⁿ, let F : ℝ → (ℝⁿ → E) be an arbitrary family of maps (F_t := F t; no continuity is assumed), and let φ : E → ℝ be continuous with compact support. Assume, as t → 0+ (along 𝓝[>] 0): (H1) eventually pr(F_t v) = v for all v ∈ K; (H2) for every ε > 0, eventually ‖F_t v − F_t v' − L(v − v')‖ ≤ ε‖v − v'‖ for all v, v' ∈ K; (H3) for every ε > 0, eventually ‖F_t v − L v‖ ≤ ε for all v ∈ K. Then ∫_{F_t(K)} φ dH → ∫_{L(K)} φ dH as t → 0+.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (K : Set (Rn n)) (pr : Amb n ℓ →L[ℝ] Rn n) (L : Rn n →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (F : ℝ → Rn n → Amb n ℓ) (φ : Amb n ℓ → ℝ), IsCompact K → Continuous φ → HasCompactSupport φ → (∀ v, pr (L v) = v) → (∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ∀ v ∈ K, pr (F t v) = v) → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ∀ v ∈ K, ∀ v' ∈ K, ‖F t v - F t v' - L (v - v')‖ ≤ ε * ‖v - v'‖) → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ∀ v ∈ K, ‖F t v - L v‖ ≤ ε) → Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => ∫ w in F t '' K, φ w ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∫ w in L '' K, φ w ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ))))
subproblem.natural_proof:
This is the measure-theoretic core of the parent proof: the finiteness of V0 (step 5), the bi-Lipschitz measure comparison and the integral estimate (steps 7-10) and the ε-argument of step 12, for a general compact K, left inverse pr and family F_t. The comparison is carried out on E with the map Φ := F_t ∘ pr (which carries H⌞L(K) onto H⌞F_t(K) up to the factors (1 ± δ)ⁿ), instead of pushing both measures to ℝⁿ by pr as in the parent's step 8; the estimates are the same. Notation: H := μHE[n] on E, H⌞X := H restricted to X, V := H(L(K)).toReal.
1. Lower bound for L. Put C := ‖pr‖ + 1 > 0 (operator norm). For every v ∈ ℝⁿ: ‖v‖ = ‖pr(L v)‖ ≤ ‖pr‖‖L v‖ ≤ C‖L v‖.
2. The plane piece. A := L(K) is compact (continuous image of a compact set), hence closed and measurable. H(A) < ∞: L is ‖L‖-Lipschitz, so the Lipschitz image bound for μHE (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn n, available under the frozen imports; equivalently LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le multiplied by the constant of euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def) gives H(A) ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ μHE[n](K); on ℝⁿ, μHE[n] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), and volume(K) < ∞ because K is compact. So V = H(A).toReal ≥ 0 is the real value of H(A).
3. The test function. Choose M ≥ 0 with |φ| ≤ M everywhere (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support); φ is uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous).
4. Parameters. Let θ > 0. By uniform continuity choose τ > 0 with |φ(a) − φ(b)| < θ/(2(V + 1)) whenever ‖a − b‖ < τ. The function d ↦ ((1 − d)⁻ⁿ − 1)(1 − d)⁻ⁿ is continuous at 0 with value 0, so we can choose δ ∈ (0, 1/2] such that κ := (1 − δ)⁻ⁿ satisfies (κ − 1)κ < θ/(4(M + 1)(V + 1)); note κ ≥ 1 and (1 + δ)ⁿ ≤ κ because (1 + δ)(1 − δ) ≤ 1.
5. The scale. The sets on which (H1) holds, on which (H2) holds with ε := δ/C, and on which (H3) holds with ε := τ/2, belong to 𝓝[>] 0, hence so does their intersection. Fix t in it. It suffices to show |∫_{F_t(K)} φ dH − ∫_{L(K)} φ dH| < θ (then Metric.tendsto_nhds gives the claim).
6. The comparison map. Define Φ : E → E by Φ(y) := F_t(pr y). Since pr(L z) = z, Φ(L z) = F_t z for every z, hence Φ(A) = F_t(K). Define Ψ : E → E by Ψ(y) := L(pr y). For z ∈ K, Ψ(Φ(L z)) = L(pr(F_t z)) = L z by (H1); so Ψ is a left inverse of Φ on A.
7. Continuity. For v, v' ∈ K, ‖F_t v − F_t v'‖ ≤ ‖F_t v − F_t v' − L(v − v')‖ + ‖L(v − v')‖ ≤ (δ/C + ‖L‖)‖v − v'‖, so F_t is Lipschitz, hence continuous, on K. Since pr is continuous and maps A into K (pr(L z) = z), Φ is continuous on A; consequently Φ is a.e.-measurable for H⌞A (ContinuousOn.aemeasurable, A measurable), and y ↦ φ(Φ y) is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞A (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable).
8. Bi-Lipschitz bounds. Let p = L z and q = L w with z, w ∈ K. Then Φ p − Φ q − (p − q) = F_t z − F_t w − L(z − w), so by (H2) and step 1, ‖Φ p − Φ q − (p − q)‖ ≤ (δ/C)‖z − w‖ ≤ δ‖L(z − w)‖ = δ‖p − q‖. By the triangle inequality, (1 − δ)‖p − q‖ ≤ ‖Φ p − Φ q‖ ≤ (1 + δ)‖p − q‖. Hence Φ is (1 + δ)-Lipschitz on A, and Ψ is (1 − δ)⁻¹-Lipschitz on Φ(A): for a = Φ p, b = Φ q we have Ψ a = p, Ψ b = q and ‖p − q‖ ≤ (1 − δ)⁻¹‖a − b‖.
9. Three finite measures. Let μ₃ := H⌞A, μ₂ := Φ_#μ₃ (Measure.map Φ μ₃) and μ₁ := H⌞Φ(A) = H⌞F_t(K). For a measurable S ⊆ E: μ₂(S) = H(Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A) (Measure.map_apply_of_aemeasurable and Measure.restrict_apply' with A measurable), μ₁(S) = H(S ∩ Φ(A)), and S ∩ Φ(A) = Φ(Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A) (Set.image_preimage_inter). (a) By the Lipschitz image bound for Φ on Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A ⊆ A: μ₁(S) ≤ (1 + δ)ⁿ μ₂(S). (b) Since Ψ is a left inverse of Φ on A, Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A = Ψ(Φ(Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A)); by the Lipschitz image bound for Ψ on Φ(Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A) ⊆ Φ(A): μ₂(S) ≤ κ μ₁(S). Hence μ₁ ≤ (1 + δ)ⁿ·μ₂ and μ₂ ≤ κ·μ₁ as measures (Measure.le_iff). Moreover μ₃(E) = μ₂(E) = H(A) < ∞ and μ₁(E) ≤ (1 + δ)ⁿ μ₂(E) < ∞, so μ₁, μ₂, μ₃ are finite, and the real value of μ₂(E) and of μ₃(E) is V.
10. Sandwich. Let g : E → ℝ be continuous with 0 ≤ g ≤ M. Then g is integrable for the finite measures μ₁, μ₂ (bounded and continuous), 0 ≤ ∫ g dμ₂ ≤ M V (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const), and by monotonicity of the integral of a nonnegative function in the measure (integral_mono_measure) together with integral_smul_measure and step 4: ∫ g dμ₁ ≤ (1 + δ)ⁿ ∫ g dμ₂ ≤ κ ∫ g dμ₂ and ∫ g dμ₂ ≤ κ ∫ g dμ₁. Therefore ∫ g dμ₁ − ∫ g dμ₂ ≤ (κ − 1)∫ g dμ₂ ≤ (κ − 1)κ M V and ∫ g dμ₂ − ∫ g dμ₁ ≤ (κ − 1)∫ g dμ₁ ≤ (κ − 1)κ ∫ g dμ₂ ≤ (κ − 1)κ M V, i.e. |∫ g dμ₁ − ∫ g dμ₂| ≤ (κ − 1)κ M V.
11. Positive and negative parts. φ = max(φ, 0) − max(−φ, 0), both parts are continuous with values in [0, M] and integrable for the finite measures μ₁, μ₂. Applying step 10 to each part: |∫ φ dμ₁ − ∫ φ dμ₂| ≤ 2(κ − 1)κ M V ≤ 2(κ − 1)κ(M + 1)(V + 1) ≤ θ/2 by step 4.
12. Change of variables. ∫ φ dμ₂ = ∫ φ(Φ y) dμ₃(y) (integral_map: Φ is a.e.-measurable for μ₃ by step 7 and φ is continuous).
13. Uniform closeness. For y = L z ∈ A (z ∈ K), ‖Φ y − y‖ = ‖F_t z − L z‖ ≤ τ/2 < τ by (H3), so |φ(Φ y) − φ(y)| < θ/(2(V + 1)). The functions y ↦ φ(Φ y) and φ are bounded by M and a.e.-strongly measurable for μ₃ (step 7), hence integrable for the finite measure μ₃, and the pointwise bound holds μ₃-a.e. because μ₃ is carried by A (ae_restrict_iff'). Therefore |∫ φ∘Φ dμ₃ − ∫ φ dμ₃| = |∫ (φ∘Φ − φ) dμ₃| ≤ θ/(2(V + 1))·V < θ/2.
14. Conclusion. ∫_{F_t(K)} φ dH = ∫ φ dμ₁ because F_t(K) = Φ(A) (step 6), and ∫_{L(K)} φ dH = ∫ φ dμ₃. Hence |∫_{F_t(K)} φ dH − ∫_{L(K)} φ dH| ≤ |∫ φ dμ₁ − ∫ φ dμ₂| + |∫ φ∘Φ dμ₃ − ∫ φ dμ₃| < θ/2 + θ/2 = θ by steps 11-13. This holds for every t in a member of 𝓝[>] 0 (step 5) and θ > 0 was arbitrary, so ∫_{F_t(K)} φ dH → ∫_{L(K)} φ dH as t → 0+.
proof_key_steps: ‖v‖ ≤ C‖L v‖ with C = ‖pr‖ + 1; A := L(K) is compact and H(A) ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ·vol(K) < ∞
fix θ > 0; choose τ from uniform continuity of φ and δ ∈ (0, 1/2] with κ = (1 − δ)⁻ⁿ and (κ − 1)κ small; take t in the eventual sets of (H1), of (H2) with ε = δ/C and of (H3) with ε = τ/2
Φ := F_t ∘ pr: Φ(L z) = F_t z, Φ(A) = F_t(K), Φ continuous and (1 ± δ)-bi-Lipschitz on A, with left inverse Ψ := L ∘ pr on A
Lipschitz image bounds: H⌞F_t(K) ≤ (1 + δ)ⁿ·Φ_#(H⌞A) and Φ_#(H⌞A) ≤ κ·H⌞F_t(K); all three measures are finite
sandwich for 0 ≤ g ≤ M and φ = φ⁺ − φ⁻: |∫ φ d(H⌞F_t(K)) − ∫ φ dΦ_#(H⌞A)| ≤ 2(κ − 1)κ M V ≤ θ/2
∫ φ dΦ_#(H⌞A) = ∫_A φ∘Φ dH and |φ∘Φ − φ| < θ/(2(V + 1)) on A by (H3), so the remaining difference is < θ/2; conclude with Metric.tendsto_nhds

audit.reason: The general compact-set contract matches its prose. H2 supplies continuity on K, the left-inverse hypotheses justify both measure comparisons, and the normalized Hausdorff image bound supplies finite mass. Restricted measurability, integrability, signed-function estimates and parameter choices are justified. H3 controls the remaining integrand error. No global regularity of F or circular tangent theorem is assumed.

subproblem.title: Two-point blow-up estimate for a C¹ map at an interior point
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝⁿ (Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) be open, let G : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Amb n ℓ) be C¹ on U (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G U), let x ∈ U, ρ ∈ ℝ and ε > 0, and put L := fderiv ℝ G x. Then for all sufficiently small t > 0, i.e. eventually along 𝓝[>] 0: (a) x + t•v ∈ U for every v in the closed ball closedBall(0, ρ) of ℝⁿ; and (b) ‖t⁻¹•(G(x + t•v) − G(x + t•v')) − L(v − v')‖ ≤ ε‖v − v'‖ for all v, v' ∈ closedBall(0, ρ).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (G : Rn n → Amb n ℓ) (x : Rn n) (ρ ε : ℝ), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G U → x ∈ U → 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), (∀ v ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) ρ, x + t • v ∈ U) ∧ ∀ v ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) ρ, ∀ v' ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) ρ, ‖t⁻¹ • (G (x + t • v) - G (x + t • v')) - fderiv ℝ G x (v - v')‖ ≤ ε * ‖v - v'‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
This is step 6 (near-linearity) of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary C¹ map on an open set. Notation: L := fderiv ℝ G x = DG(x), DG(z) := fderiv ℝ G z.
1. Regularity. Since U is open and G is C¹ on U, G is differentiable at every z ∈ U (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn with 1 ≠ 0, then DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt using U ∈ 𝓝 z), and z ↦ DG(z) is continuous on U (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, 1 ≤ 1).
2. A good ball. Choose δ₀ > 0 with ball(x, δ₀) ⊆ U (U open; Metric.isOpen_iff) and δ₁ > 0 such that ‖DG(z) − L‖ < ε for every z ∈ U with dist(z, x) < δ₁ (continuity of DG at x within U; Metric.continuousOn_iff). Put δ := min(δ₀, δ₁) > 0. Then every z ∈ ball(x, δ) lies in U and satisfies ‖DG(z) − L‖ ≤ ε.
3. The scales. The interval (0, δ/(|ρ| + 1)) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT); fix t in it. For v ∈ closedBall(0, ρ) we have ‖v‖ ≤ ρ ≤ |ρ| < |ρ| + 1, hence ‖(x + t•v) − x‖ = t‖v‖ ≤ t(|ρ| + 1) < δ, i.e. x + t•v ∈ ball(x, δ) ⊆ U. This proves (a) for this t. (If ρ < 0 the closed ball is empty and (a), (b) hold vacuously; the argument below covers this case too.)
4. An auxiliary map. Define h : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ}, h(v) := t⁻¹•G(x + t•v) − L v. Let v ∈ closedBall(0, ρ) and z := x + t•v ∈ ball(x, δ) ⊆ U. The affine map v ↦ x + t•v has derivative t•id, and G is differentiable at z (step 1), so by the chain rule h has derivative t⁻¹•(DG(z) ∘ (t•id)) − L = DG(x + t•v) − L at v (HasFDerivAt.comp, HasFDerivAt.const_smul, HasFDerivAt.sub, using t⁻¹·t = 1). By step 2 its operator norm is at most ε.
5. Mean value inequality. closedBall(0, ρ) is convex, and h has, at every point of it, a derivative of norm ≤ ε (step 4, passing from HasFDerivAt to HasFDerivWithinAt). By Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasFDerivWithin_le, ‖h v − h v'‖ ≤ ε‖v − v'‖ for all v, v' ∈ closedBall(0, ρ).
6. Conclusion. By linearity of L and of t⁻¹•(·), h v − h v' = t⁻¹•(G(x + t•v) − G(x + t•v')) − L(v − v'). With step 5 this is (b). Since (a) and (b) hold for every t in the member (0, δ/(|ρ| + 1)) of 𝓝[>] 0, the conjunction holds eventually along 𝓝[>] 0.
proof_key_steps: C¹ on the open set U: G is differentiable on U and z ↦ DG(z) is continuous on U
choose δ > 0 with ball(x, δ) ⊆ U and ‖DG(z) − L‖ ≤ ε on ball(x, δ)
for 0 < t < δ/(|ρ| + 1) and v ∈ closedBall(0, ρ): x + t•v ∈ ball(x, δ) ⊆ U, which is (a)
h(v) := t⁻¹•G(x + t•v) − L v has derivative DG(x + t•v) − L of norm ≤ ε on closedBall(0, ρ) (chain rule)
mean value inequality on the convex closed ball, and h v − h v' = t⁻¹•(G(x + t•v) − G(x + t•v')) − L(v − v'), give (b)

audit.reason: All hypotheses and quantifiers match. The positive scale bound ensures domain membership and derivative control; t > 0 justifies derivative cancellation. The convex mean-value inequality then gives the exact two-point estimate. Arbitrary radii, including empty negative-radius balls, are covered. The proof is complete and independent of the parent and siblings.

subproblem.title: Set integrals of a function vanishing off B agree on sets that agree inside B
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Amb n ℓ), φ : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ, and S, T, B ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with B measurable, φ(w) = 0 for every w ∉ B, S ∩ B ⊆ T and T ⊆ S. Then ∫_S φ dμ = ∫_T φ dμ (Bochner set integrals; no integrability of φ and no measurability of S or T is assumed).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (φ : Amb n ℓ → ℝ) (S T B : Set (Amb n ℓ)), MeasurableSet B → (∀ w, w ∉ B → φ w = 0) → S ∩ B ⊆ T → T ⊆ S → ∫ w in S, φ w ∂μ = ∫ w in T, φ w ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
This is the integral identity used in step 11 (localization) of the parent proof, for a general measure μ.
1. Since φ vanishes outside B, φ equals its indicator B.indicator φ pointwise: for w ∈ B both equal φ(w) (Set.indicator_of_mem), and for w ∉ B both equal 0 (Set.indicator_of_notMem and the hypothesis).
2. For every set X ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}: ∫_X φ dμ = ∫ (B.indicator φ) d(μ⌞X) = ∫_B φ d(μ⌞X) = ∫_{B ∩ X} φ dμ. The middle equality is MeasureTheory.integral_indicator for the measurable set B applied to the measure μ⌞X; it holds without any integrability assumption (if φ is not integrable on the relevant set, both sides are 0 by convention). The last equality is Measure.restrict_restrict with B measurable: (μ⌞X)⌞B = μ⌞(B ∩ X).
3. B ∩ S = B ∩ T. If w ∈ B ∩ S, then w ∈ S ∩ B ⊆ T, so w ∈ B ∩ T. If w ∈ B ∩ T, then w ∈ S because T ⊆ S, so w ∈ B ∩ S.
4. By steps 2 and 3, ∫_S φ dμ = ∫_{B ∩ S} φ dμ = ∫_{B ∩ T} φ dμ = ∫_T φ dμ.
proof_key_steps: φ = B.indicator φ because φ vanishes off B
for any X: ∫_X φ dμ = ∫_{B ∩ X} φ dμ (integral_indicator, Measure.restrict_restrict; no integrability needed)
B ∩ S = B ∩ T from S ∩ B ⊆ T ⊆ S

audit.reason: The proof establishes the full stated generality. Measurability of B suffices for integral_indicator and the required order of restrict_restrict; neither integrability nor measurability of S and T is needed. The two inclusions imply equality of their intersections with B, completing the exact integral identity.
